posts.title: Weighted Least Squares
posts.excerpt: Plain least squares gives a cheap multimeter the same vote as a precise bench meter. Weighted Least Squares gives every measurement a weight based on how noisy it is: a noisy meter gets a quiet voice, a precise meter a loud one.
sheetImages: assets/img/posts/least-squares/Weighted Least Squares — Robotics Concepts in One Page_page-0001.jpg

posts.title: Least Squares
posts.excerpt: Least squares is basically a way of taking many imperfect measurements of the same thing and finding the one answer that disagrees with all of them the least. The older, simpler idea underneath the Kalman filter.
sheetImages: assets/img/posts/least-squares/Least Squares — Robotics Concepts in One Page_page-0001.jpg

posts.title: ESKF: The Mathematics
posts.excerpt: To actually understand how the ESKF works — not just the idea behind it — we walk through the math step by step: propagate, linearize, update, correct, reset.
sheetImages: assets/img/posts/kalman/ESKF The Mathematics — Robotics Concepts in One Page_page-0001.jpg

posts.title: The Error State Kalman Filter
posts.excerpt: The regular Kalman Filter assumes everything behaves linearly. Real robots don't. The ESKF linearizes the small error around the current estimate, bringing nonlinear systems back into Kalman territory.
sheetImages: assets/img/posts/kalman/Error State Kalman Filter — Robotics Concepts in One Page_page-0001.jpg

posts.title: Linear Kalman Filter
posts.excerpt: The Kalman filter is basically a tool used to combine information from different sources to get a more accurate estimate of something. Starting the series with a self-driving car case study.
sheetImages: assets/img/posts/kalman/Linear Kalman Filter — Robotics Concepts in One Page_page-0001.jpg
